title: Canonical strict open mate and its scalar and completed endpoints
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with adic datum $d$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let $v:U'\to U$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $g:T'\to T$ be an open Cartesian square $s$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Use the ordinary and completed derived pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], completed reduction towers [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], the specified simultaneous strict open exchange [def-cbc-completed-strict-open-exchange], and the completed inverse-limit functor [def-pur-completed-rlim-functor]. This node records the following already constructed canonical data, in the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $Q=G_g^{\rm actual}Q_Tj_!$ and $Q'=J_{j'}^{\rm actual}G_v^{\rm actual}Q_U$, and define $\Omega:Q\simeq Q'$ by the canonical quotient/open identification followed by the actual strict exchange. Let $r_W$ be restriction from completed quotient towers to constant-$A$ towers. Put $M=r_UQ_U$, $N=G_gJ_jM$ and $N'=J_{j'}G_vM$. Define $a:r_{T'}Q\simeq N$ and $b:r_{T'}Q'\simeq N'$ by the existing actual-to-datum pullback, scalar/pullback, scalar/open, and quotient/open comparisons, in their displayed source and target orders. Define $\beta_s(K):N(K)\simeq N'(K)$ to be the specified constant-$A$ strict open-unit mate at $M(K)$. When $j$ is quasi-compact, let $q_s$ be the induced quasi-compactness structure on $j'$ obtained by base change. Define $\widehat a_K:r_{T'}L g^*_{\rm comp}j_!K\simeq R\lim N(K)$ as the scalar/pullback-limit comparison followed by $R\lim$ of the quotient/open comparison. Define $\widehat b_K:r_{T'}j'_!L v^*_{\rm comp}K\simeq J_{j'}R\lim G_vM(K)$ as scalar/open comparison followed by $J_{j'}$ of scalar/pullback-limit comparison. These are precisely cbcOpenMateSource, cbcOpenMateTarget, cbcOpenMateOmega, cbcOpenMateM, cbcOpenMateN, cbcOpenMateN', cbcOpenMateA, cbcOpenMateB, cbcOpenMateBeta, cbcOpenMateQC, cbcOpenMateCompletedA and cbcOpenMateCompletedB in the published module. Their data are the indicated composites of the fixed comparisons, with no arbitrary endpoint isomorphisms; this definition asserts neither the strict-mate identification nor its completed-limit equality.
